QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_16

question.text: A Category II AIF reports a Fund IRR of 35% and a Direct Alpha of 10%. What is the implied IRR of the public-market index used as the benchmark?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7.3.6 (Example 7.4): Fund IRR = Market IRR + Direct Alpha. Therefore Market IRR = Fund IRR - Direct Alpha = 35% - 10% = 25%. Direct Alpha is the excess annualised IRR over the benchmark's pace-matched IRR. The Trap: 45% adds instead of subtracting. 3.5% divides. 35% just copies fund IRR. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical formula. Classic CFA GIPS-style alpha is computed differently (using CAPM beta) — don't confuse with Direct Alpha (market-pace IRR subtraction). Manager's Pro-Tip: Report BOTH KS-PME and Direct Alpha in every half-yearly LP letter — institutional LPs (pension funds, SWFs) request both, and computing only one signals incomplete benchmarking discipline.
